data.gender_notes: Manvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manvika is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘manas’ meaning mind, intellect. It is believed to signify the embodiment of wisdom and intelligence. In Hindu mythology, Manvantara is the current world cycle ruled by Manu, the lawgiver and savior of mankind. The name Manvika carries the meaning “Mind, intellect” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manvika usually hope their child will grow to embody mind, intellect and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Manvika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mind, intellect.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manvika total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Manvika has rich cultural significance in Hinduism. It reflects the importance of knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom in Hindu society. The name reverberates the values embedded in Hindu literature, philosophy, and education. Moreover, the name has strong associations with the Hindu god, Manu, who symbolizes creation, law, order, and righteousness.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the name Manvika signifies the embodiment of the Divine Intellect or Buddhi in an individual. It is a reminder of the ultimate goal of human life, which is to attain divine knowledge, understanding, and transcendence beyond the limitations of the mind. The name inspires one to cultivate wisdom through learning, meditation, and self-reflection. It also evokes the virtues of humility, compassion, and detachment, essential qualities for spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manvika: One who embodies the wisdom and knowledge of Manav (Mankind). Carrying the legacy of collective human consciousness, she inspires growth and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Manvika is considered the sister of Manav, the first man on Earth according to Hindu mythology. She is also known as the mother of Manav's wife Shraddha and the 71 other wives.
historical_references.time_period: Prehistoric, around the beginning of human civilization (according to Hindu mythology)
historical_references.context: Manvantara, the seventh Manvantara or world cycle, in Hindu cosmology.

historical_references.reference: Manvika is also a name of the goddesses Parvati and Lakshmi in some Hindu traditions, symbolizing the aspects of love and prosperity respectively.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient to Medieval Period, 3rd millennium BCE to 13th century CE
historical_references.context: Devotional and Puranic literature, particularly in the Shiva and Vishnu traditions.
